The incident comes amid a surge of ICE activity
in California that started in early October and
has led to multiple hospitalizations. Days earlier,
agents broke the arm of Ricardo Gonzalez, also a
US citizen, in Long Beach. In videos, Gonzalez
appears face-down in a gutter crying out for
help while officers kneel on his back.

In the Bay Area, two separate ICE arrests also led
to hospitalizations, sparking anti-ICE protests
outside of an Oakland hospital.

Glenn Goldin, is a retired special education
teacher who formerlv taught Zepeda and
remains a close mentor to him. He described
Zepeda, who lives in a group home for adults
with disabilities. as quiet sensitive and a caring
housemate. who loves the Golden State Warriors
and likes to spend time scrolling TikTok.

After Zepeda's terrifying encounter with ICE,
Goldin said that he remains shaken and doesn't
plan to return to school for at least several
weeks.

Goldin said Zepeda had worked up the courage
to begin walking to school by himself last year.

"He's felt very proud of himself, you know, he's
independent." Goldin said. "I feel like thev took
that awav from him."

In the 20 minutes before ICE officers detained
Zepeda, they had already pulled over two
separate dark-skinned drivers and then let them
go, according to the observer, who provided
videos of both encounters to the Guardian.

The first ICE stop occurred around 7:08 am. Two
ICE vehicles were stopped alongside a Santa
Maria road as agents questioned a driver. After
the agents drove away, the driver - who the
observer said was a Hispanic man - can be heard
saying to the observer. "I'm a US citizen" in a
video reviewed by the Guardian.

About 10 minutes later one of the same ICE
vehicles pulled over a truck with two people
inside and then let them go, the observer's video
shows. The observer said they appeared to be
Latino men.
